To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TCR triggering induces the formation of Lck–actinin-1–RACK1 multiprotein complex that affects Lck redistribution.

RACK1, an adaptor protein that interacts with activated Lck, is essential for the formation of multiprotein complex that includes cytoskeleton proteins and affects Lck redistribution in primary CD4 T-cells.
RACK1 is an essential component of a multiprotein signaling complex that links kinase active Lck with cytoskeletal network in primary CD4 T-cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a multiprotein complex that is involved in the process of Lck redistribution and activation.
the formation of a complex network of proteins that are essential for T-cell activation and function.
understanding the molecular basis for the activation-induced redistribution of the Src-family kinase, Lck.

RACK1 is a novel adaptor protein that is essential for TCR-triggered Lck redistribution and the formation of the RACK1–actinin-1–pY-kinase active Lck complex is critical to the formation of a functional signaling hub.
TCR triggering induces the formation of a RACK1 multiprotein network that affects Lck redistribution and its function.
the RACK1–actin network is a critical element of TCR-induced signaling that regulates Lck redistribution and its function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formation of Lck-RACK1-actinin-2 multiprotein network is a key step for the initiation of productive T cell signaling and cytoskeleton rearrangement upon TCR triggering.

the multiprotein complex, including RACK1, α-actin-1, and pY394LCK, serves as a signal hub that regulates the redistribution of kinase active LCK in TCR-activated T cells.

the formation of Lck–α-Actinin-1–RACK1 complex serves as an early event in the TCR-induced signaling cascade that regulates the redistribution of the Lck kinase and affects the formation of a complex signaling network.
